input_file.description: Absolute path to the source .xlsx workbook.

output_file.description: Absolute path where the corrected workbook is written.

answer_position.description: A1-style cell that currently holds the error, e.g. 'B7'.

solution_contract.description: Required artifacts, e.g. 'Write solution.py and case1_result.xlsx. solution.py uses INPUT_PATH and OUTPUT_PATH.'

files.description: Workspace-relative published files, including solution.py and the corrected workbook.

solution_py.description: Publication name of the emitted runner script (e.g. solution.py).

result_workbook.description: Publication name of the corrected workbook (e.g. case1_result.xlsx).

repaired_value.description: The formula or literal now stored in the target cell.

skills.entry_constraints: Input must exist as an .xlsx workbook. answer_position is an A1-style cell reference such as 'B7'. The program reads INPUT_PATH and writes OUTPUT_PATH, and must publish solution.py and the corrected workbook as workspace-relative names. Only the error scope may be altered; unrelated cells, sheets and styles are preserved.
skills.name: Repair an error cell (e.g. #REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #N/A) at a caller-specified A1 answer position in an .xlsx workbook, producing a corrected workbook where the target cell is no longer an error plus a reusable openpyxl-based runner script.
skills.guidance: Repair an error cell (e.g. #REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #N/A) at a caller-specified A1 answer position in an .xlsx workbook, producing a corrected workbook where the target cell is no longer an error plus a reusable openpyxl-based runner script.

skills.entry_constraints: Requires openpyxl; INPUT_PATH/OUTPUT_PATH may be injected by the sandbox. The result workbook and the generating script must be published as workspace-relative files (no leading slash, no inputs/ prefix). Row count and column count are derived from target_range; total cells must equal the number of source values.
skills.name: Given an .xlsx whose source values sit in a single column, reshape that column into a rectangular block anchored at a specified start cell (e.g. B2) using the symmetrical/alternating-direction (serpentine) row order that keeps the arrangement visually symmetric, and publish the resulting workbook plus the Python script that produced it.
skills.guidance: Given an .xlsx whose source values sit in a single column, reshape that column into a rectangular block anchored at a specified start cell (e.g. B2) using the symmetrical/alternating-direction (serpentine) row order that keeps the arrangement visually symmetric, and publish the resulting workbook plus the Python script that produced it.

skills.entry_constraints: input_file must exist and be a readable .xlsx; answer_position must be writable cells in the same sheet as the data/flags; the chosen formula must be supported by the evaluation engine (Excel and/or LibreOffice).
skills.name: Given an .xlsx workbook with a data table plus designated input flag cells and answer cells, author and apply an Excel formula that lists the row labels (e.g. customer names) whose flags match a required value, and publish a solution.py and the recalculated result workbook.
skills.guidance: Given an .xlsx workbook with a data table plus designated input flag cells and answer cells, author and apply an Excel formula that lists the row labels (e.g. customer names) whose flags match a required value, and publish a solution.py and the recalculated result workbook.

skills.entry_constraints: input_file must exist and be a readable .xlsx workbook; the source column must contain an ordered sequence of dates or numbers whose expected step is inferable; source and target columns must be within worksheet bounds.
skills.name: Given a spreadsheet whose source column holds a date (or numeric) sequence, detect the values missing from the expected contiguous sequence and write them into a target column of a result workbook, returning the updated workbook as the deliverable.
skills.guidance: Given a spreadsheet whose source column holds a date (or numeric) sequence, detect the values missing from the expected contiguous sequence and write them into a target column of a result workbook, returning the updated workbook as the deliverable.

input_file.description: Workbook path containing the main data sheet (name, contact number, mail ID, designation, location) and the empty result sheet.

output_file.description: Path to write the completed workbook.

answer_position.description: Target range on the result sheet to fill, e.g. "'result'!B2:D12".

skills.entry_constraints: The input workbook must exist and contain a main data sheet with name, contact number, mail ID, designation and location fields plus a result sheet holding the given answer range. Program must read INPUT_PATH, write OUTPUT_PATH, emit solution.py, and publish the completed result workbook.
skills.name: Fill a target Excel result sheet by conditionally looking up each person's details from a main data sheet: for records whose designation matches the requested criteria for the given location, write the person's name against their location together with contact details and mail ID; write 'N/A' in the cells when the designation does not match; and left-align all output cells.
skills.guidance: Fill a target Excel result sheet by conditionally looking up each person's details from a main data sheet: for records whose designation matches the requested criteria for the given location, write the person's name against their location together with contact details and mail ID; write 'N/A' in the cells when the designation does not match; and left-align all output cells.

skills.entry_constraints: Requires Python with openpyxl (or equivalent) to read/write .xlsx. Single source workbook; answer_position is an A1-style range. Numeric parsing must be robust to currency symbols and to both '.' and ',' being present.
skills.name: Given an Excel workbook whose cells hold currency-formatted text strings (symbols/numbers in varying positions and formats), extract the numeric value from each target-cell string, determine the valid decimal sign ('.' vs ',') for that string, and write the parsed numbers into the specified answer range of the output workbook.
skills.guidance: Given an Excel workbook whose cells hold currency-formatted text strings (symbols/numbers in varying positions and formats), extract the numeric value from each target-cell string, determine the valid decimal sign ('.' vs ',') for that string, and write the parsed numbers into the specified answer range of the output workbook.

skills.entry_constraints: input_file must exist and be a readable .xlsx; destination_range must lie within the sheet or the sheet must be extendable; duplicate detection is per-row and exact-value based, preserving first occurrence order.
skills.name: Deduplicate repeated values within each spreadsheet row (not column-wise): read a source range or the used part of a sheet, remove later occurrences of any value already seen in the same row while preserving first-occurrence order, and write the deduplicated row-wise result into a specified destination range of an output workbook.
skills.guidance: Deduplicate repeated values within each spreadsheet row (not column-wise): read a source range or the used part of a sheet, remove later occurrences of any value already seen in the same row while preserving first-occurrence order, and write the deduplicated row-wise result into a specified destination range of an output workbook.
